200.description:
One record by the source's own identity (the batch's `records/get`): the source abbreviation plus the file's `id`. The download has no per-record endpoint, so the function reads the current file in Range segments until the `SOURCE:id` key matches (up to the whole 34 MB, 20-80 s for a late source such as UVL) and fails with not_found when the key is not in the current publication. Non-Treasury ids are content hashes that change when the agency edits the record, so a not_found for an id taken from an older snapshot usually means the row changed, not that the party was removed.

The response contains the tool result directly.

200.description:
The full current list (the batch's `records/list`), paginated with a cursor pinned to one publication. Every page re-reads the file's trailer, recomputes the publication id and compares it with the one in the cursor; when the source moved on the call fails with invalid_input whose issue code is `publication_changed` (message prefixed `publication_changed:`), never mixing publications. Pages are read as Range segments of the 34 MB consolidated.json from the pinned byte offset; on resume the last record of the previous page is re-read and its `SOURCE:id` checked against the cursor, so a re-ordered file is also reported as publication_changed. Filters: `sources` (list abbreviations; ISN is accepted for ACN), `exclude_treasury` (drops SDN, SSI, FSE, CAP, CMIC, MBS, PLC, which `sanctionssearch-ofac-treas-gov` already covers), `entity_types`, `programs` (exact program strings). A page reads until `limit` records matched or the file ended (the whole 34 MB file scans in under 10 s), so a filtered page shorter than `limit` normally means the list is exhausted; `next_cursor` is null exactly when it is. Records are grouped by source in the file (ACN first, SDN the bulk, UVL last on 2026-10-17) but no order is promised.

The response contains the tool result directly.

content_hash.description: Also compute the content hash of every record (reads the whole 34 MB file).

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Version check of the current consolidated.json (the batch's `source/status`; named with an underscore because function names must be identifiers). One Range request for the file's trailer returns the publication id (SHA-256 over the sorted `source=source_last_updated` lines of `sources_used` plus the record total: it moves only when an agency publishes or the count changes, unlike the ETag, Last-Modified and `search_performed_at`, which change at every hourly rebuild), the build time, the per-source import state, the record count, the JSON/CSV/TSV file URLs and the JSON size. The publisher posts no hash; with `content_hash: true` the function walks the whole file in Range segments (about 34 MB, 30-90 s) and returns the SHA-256 of the sorted per-record canonical SHA-256 digests, an order-independent hash of the records themselves.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content_hash` | string | Hex SHA-256 over the sorted SHA-256 digests of every record's canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace); null unless `content_hash` was requested. |
| `content_hash_algorithm` | string |  |
| `content_hash_records` | number | Records that went into the content hash; null unless requested. |
| `etag` | string | The file's ETag; rotates at every hourly rebuild. |
| `file_url` | string |  |
| `file_urls` | object[] |  |
| `last_modified` | string |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `publication_id` | string | Hex SHA-256 fingerprint of the publication (see the function description). The value `records_list` pins its cursor to. |
| `published_at` | string | The file's `search_performed_at`: when this hourly build was made (ISO 8601 with offset). |
| `publisher_hash` | object | Always null: trade.gov posts no checksum for the files. |
| `record_count` | number | The file's `total`. |
| `size_bytes` | number | Size of consolidated.json in bytes. |
| `source_url` | string |  |
